identityReview: Nawaf Salam, Lebanese jurist/academic/diplomat, born Beirut December 15, 1953. Sorbonne history doctorate 1979, Lebanese law Licence 1984, Harvard LL.M. 1991, Sciences Po political-science Doctorat d’Etat 1992; 1974 EHESS diplôme not relabelled bachelor. AUB associate professor/department chair and Harvard visiting research distinct. UN representative July 2007–2017, monthly Security Council chair May 2010/September 2011. ICJ judge from February 6, 2018 and court president February 6, 2024; resigned effective January 14, 2025 after January 13 government-formation designation. Cabinet February 8 and confidence February 26; current prime minister, not current ICJ president or ICC president.
lifeStatusEvidence: English MTV and original Arabic Elnashra November 16, 2026 reports describe completed Grand Serail meeting with World Bank delegation led by Anna Bjerde, attended by ministers. Policy promises and requested acceleration not measured outcomes. November 17 family-travel notice is prospective/private and not adopted as a completed trip or personal health claim.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read specified UN candidate-CV pages, current government-affiliated finance-institute biography, complete UN judicial-vacancy note, relevant government-formation paragraph of Secretary-General report, IDEA tracker/update, LBCI confidence report, World Bank LEAP approval body, MTV English and Elnashra Arabic recent meeting. corrections: Read Nawaf Salam candidate CV on printed pages 50–51 of UN A/72/183–S/2017/621: Lebanese citizen, Beirut December 15, 1953; history PhD Sorbonne 1979, Lebanese University law Licence/LLB 1984, Harvard LL.M. 1991, Sciences Po Doctorat d’Etat 1992, plus 1979 DEA and 1974 EHESS Diplôme. Do not convert the latter to a confirmed bachelor degree. Beirut Bar practice 1984–1989/1992–2007, Boston 1989–1992; Harvard visiting research not tenure. AUB associate professor 2003–2007 and department chair 2005–2007. UN ambassador from July 2007; Security Council rotating presidencies May 2010/September 2011, not continuous two-year presidency or UN Secretary-General. Electoral commission member and rapporteur 2005–2006, not automatically enacted reform or title copied from secondary Secretary-General wording. Other candidates’ biographies and original diplomas not independently authenticated.

Read current Lebanese Institut des Finances profile: prime minister since February 8, 2025, former UN representative 2007–2017, ICJ member from 2018, elected court president 2024 and resignation after designation. Its “for a nine-year term” wording describes scheduled appointment, not nine years actually completed; exact resignation dates from UN Secretary-General supersede ambiguous shorthand. Three major postgraduate degrees corroborated. No unverified ordinal numbering, political-family role or simultaneous current judicial office adopted.

Read full two-page UN Secretary-General S/2025/37, dated January 16, 2025: resignation letter dated January 13, effective January 14, vacancy that day. Judicial service began February 6, 2018; elected/appointed court president February 6, 2024; original judicial term due February 5, 2027. Do not confuse letter/publication/effective dates, judge term with presidency term, or ICJ with ICC. Original ICJ press releases inaccessible; no claim of reading those files or individual judicial case records.

Read paragraph 54 of UN Secretary-General S/2025/153 (March 12, 2025 report): January 13 binding consultations/designation, 84 of 128 MPs supporting candidate, February 8 cabinet decree, 24 ministers including five women. Report date is not appointment date. Only relevant paragraphs inspected; do not claim full conflict annex/complete report audit. Reform-and-rescue label and expressed aspirations are not independently verified completed reform or final peace settlement.

Read International IDEA January 2025 tracker and February update: Aoun elected January 9, Salam designated January 13, cabinet February 8, confidence February 26 with 95 votes. Report is institutional secondary synthesis with cited journalism. Expected 2026 parliamentary elections are historical expectation, not verified current event; no assertion about whether those elections occurred. Distinguish 84 designation supporters from 95 later confidence votes and 128 total seats.

Read LBCI February 26, 2025 concise report: two days debating ministerial statement, 95 votes in favour of confidence. Not a direct popular election and not the same procedure as January nomination. Dynamic surrounding news are unrelated and do not change article date. No full parliamentary roll-call, abstention count or complete policy statement claimed.

Read relevant full World Bank June 25, 2025 release body: Board approved yesterday, so June 24; US$250 million financing for LEAP and expandable US$1 billion framework. Infrastructure/services/rubble work, PM office strategic guidance, Public Works and Transport implementation, Environment oversight. Approval, framework size, additional future grants/loans and actual disbursement are distinct. No personal payment, already completed reconstruction or independent 2026 implementation audit inferred from original approval. Avoid mistaking article date for Board decision date.

Read MTV English November 16, 2026 completed World Bank meeting account: Anna Bjerde, Ousmane Dione, Enrique Blanco Armas and ministers meet Salam at Grand Serail; LEAP, GATE, digitalisation, energy and regional links discussed. Call for accelerated projects and studies is advocacy, not established completion. Not the Turkish president personally visiting because a different report mentions Bilal Erdoğan; not new cabinet appointment.

Read Elnashra original Arabic November 16, 2026 article to cross-check English: actual World Bank delegation, relevant ministers, LEAP/GATE/digital projects, energy and economic connectivity, promise of continuing financial/economic/administrative reforms and faster project implementation. No numerical disbursement claim made. Government site matching original announcement found in search but timed out on open, so do not claim primary full statement was read.
